title.narrative: Early Action Integrated Food Crisis Response to Food Security Crisis in North Darfur State, Sudan

description.narrative: ltpgtThe project will be implemented by COOPI and UPO in Mellit locality which is located about 65 km from El Fasher town, North Darfur state, Sudan. The two partners owe several years of operational experience in North Darfur and have well established offices and staff on the ground. The proposed action will target Mellit, a total direct beneficiary of 17,977 individuals including women, men, boys, girls and people with disability out with a focus on newly internally displaced persons (IDPs) forced to flee their homes/origin areas after 15 April 2023 due to ongoing Sudan war. ltbrgtThe war between Sudan’s army and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) has been especially hard on Darfur region, which had already experienced several periods of armed conflict over the past two decades. At communal level, the new arrivals have settled in a frame of pre- existing tensions and episodes of violence over resources. Although there are other factors driving conflict in the targeted areas, there is a predominance of land, pasture and water resource control driven conflict. ltbrgtDuring the past years, clashes have been registered between farmers and pastoralists due to limited access to water sources and consequently damage to agricultural fields by cattle, in ND. These conflicts easily escalate into ethnic conflicts among groups who already have a history of violent conflict and mistrust. The ongoing Sudanese war and the dispute over Darfur between RSF and SAF, has exacerbated this situation. Economic disruption, restriction of movements, lack of access to basic services are mixing up with pre- existing tensions over the scarce resources.Pastoral communities and farmers, due to the market disruption caused by the war and the restriction of access, is being unable to secure or afford essential agricultural inputs, including fuel and fertilizer, thus jeopardizing the upcoming planting season, and in turn the food security status of the population of the area.ltbrgtAs farmers will be advised to plant less, adopt cash-crop production, or assume alternative livelihood activities, this will lead to reduced yields impacting in turn food availability and all four dimensions pertinent to food security – food availability, food access, utilization and stability, which are all currently endangered. Additionally, newly arrivals, families which completely loss their means of sustainability are captured in a vicious cycle of poverty. This proposal is aiming at tackle the extremely food insecurity level (and projected) through a holistic, integrated and conflict sensitivity approach, targeting the most at risk, vulnerable social groups inside IDPs and Hosting Communities, in the rural area of Mellit. ltbrgtlt/pgt
